transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (BrightCart PM), Samir Gupta (BrightCart Platform), Leah Brooks (BrightCart Head of AI)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC results and next steps for canary and cutover. Covered monitoring, rollback/runbook, A/B vs canary strategy, required infra changes (VPC peering, egress rules), and a draft schedule for the 2-hour canary window. Agreed action items and owners.

Topics:
- Canary rollout plan and verification
- A/B vs canary trade-offs
- Monitoring & alerting (logs, traces, latency, error budget)
- Runbooks and rollback criteria
- Data handling (KMS, audit logs, retention)
- Post-canary metrics and rollout cadence

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we have Alex, Samir, Leah, Maya and me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex: Doing good, thanks. excited to get through the rollout checklist.
[00:12] Maya: morning all. I pulled the latest perf numbers from the POC runs last night.
[00:18] Samir: yep saw those — latency looks decent but we have a couple of tail spikes we need to talk about.
[00:24] Leah: the quality is pretty solid on our 3 main prompts; two edge prompts still hallucinate a bit.
[00:30] Jordan: perfect, let's start with canary strategy. we originally proposed a canary + automatic fallback to a cheaper hosted variant if error rate climbs. thoughts?
[00:45] Samir: we prefer canary to A/B for infra simplicity. we can do a warm pool 10% traffic to Redwood, rest on current system, then ramp. need VPC peering set up and a fixed egress IP for allowlisting.
[00:58] Maya: agree. from SE side we'll instrument request-level tracing and a metric for prompt-level correctness via the eval set you gave.
[01:10] Alex: what are the exact success thresholds? latency P50, P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens?
[01:18] Leah: i sent a draft earlier: target P95 < 450ms, P50 < 120ms, error rate < 1.5% on production prompts, and model quality pass rate >= 95% on the eval set.
[01:33] Jordan: okay good. we'll bake those into the canary runbook. Maya, you mentioned tail spikes — can you summarize?
[01:40] Maya: sure. we saw a couple P99 spikes up to 1.6s during concurrent long-context calls. looks related to KV cache warmup and batching behavior. can tune batch window but that trades latency/rate.
[01:52] Samir: important we don't break user facing flows. what does rollback look like?
[01:58] Jordan: rollback is immediate traffic shift back to current endpoint plus invalidating local cache. we also have an automatic fallback policy where if error rate > 2% for 5 minutes or P95 > 700ms, routing falls back to the hosted model variant.
[02:15] Alex: can we automate alerts to Ops and also create a Slack incident channel?
[02:19] Maya: yes. we'll hook up CloudWatch/Prometheus alerts to an Ops channel, and send a runbook link in the alert payload.
[02:28] Leah: about auditing and security — our compliance team needs KMS integration and audit logs retained for 90 days. is Redwood's private deployment KMS compatible?
[02:36] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we'll include the KMS config snippet in the runbook. audit logs are configurable, default retention 30 days but can be extended to 90 on request — we'll capture that as part of the contract.
[02:50] Samir: network wise we need: VPC peering, egress IPs, and ensure no outbound to arbitrary third parties. also need a plan for secrets — do you support HSM?
[02:59] Maya: we integrate with common KMS providers and HSM options for enterprise. secrets are loaded via the control plane with ephemeral tokens for the runtime. we'll share detailed network and secret docs.
[03:12] Alex: can we walk through a sample canary timeline? what are the steps minute-by-minute in the 2 hour window?
[03:20] Jordan: propose: 0-10m pre-checks (infra, peering, keys), 10-20m start 5% traffic, 20-40m monitor metrics, 40-60m ramp to 20% if green, 60-90m run additional load tests and manual QA, 90-110m 50% traffic if all good, 110-120m final decision to cutover or rollback.
[03:45] Samir: sounds okay, but we want an option to pause ramping and keep at 20% for extra monitoring. also need a smoke test that hits our top 10 critical prompts.
[03:56] Maya: noted — we'll include a smoke test harness. Maya: also will include synthetic load generator with the same token distribution as your production traffic.
[04:06] Leah: how are we measuring quality continuously? can we do automated accuracy checks on returning responses?
[04:12] Maya: we'll run responses against the eval suite and metrics collector; also set alerts on regression delta exceeding 2% for key prompts.
[04:21] Jordan: one tradeoff we discussed earlier is A/B vs canary for quality assessment — A/B gives direct user impact measurement but doubles infra. thoughts?
[04:31] Alex: A/B is attractive to product but cost is a concern. for go-live we prefer canary with a short A/B experiment later once stable.
[04:39] Samir: agreed. from infra ops, canary minimizes risk.
[04:44] Jordan: ok let's go with canary first, then a small A/B for feature flags in 2 weeks.
[04:50] Alex: any legal/procurement blockers?
[04:53] Leah: procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence and a DPA addendum; we got the earlier security deck but need the certificate and an updated DPA.
[04:59] Jordan: i'll have our security lead send the SOC2 cert and the DPA template by EOD Friday.
[05:05] Samir: what about rate limiting and protective throttles? we don't want a noisy tenant to take down the canary.
[05:11] Maya: we can enable per-customer rate limits and circuit breakers — configured in the routing policy. we'll propose safe defaults in the runbook.
[05:19] Alex: last question — post-canary metrics to review?
[05:22] Jordan: we'll report P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, quality pass rate on eval prompts, token costs per 1k, and any incidents. recommended review cadence: 24h, 72h, and 1 week.
[05:34] Leah: fine. also want a post-mortem template if anything happens.
[05:38] Jordan: included.
[05:40] Alex: ok, next steps?
[05:42] Jordan: Redwood to share canary runbook and monitoring playbook by Friday (2026-11-27). BrightCart to provide final prompt list, VPC peering details, and sign-off timeline by Monday (2026-11-29). schedule canary for 2026-12-02 02:00-04:00 PST — tentative.
[05:58] Samir: we'll confirm peering and egress IPs by Monday.
[06:01] Leah: procurement will review SOC2 + DPA, expect feedback early next week.
[06:06] Jordan: perfect, we'll send a calendar invite for the canary window and include SE join. thanks everyone.
[06:12] Alex: thanks all.

Meeting end.
